title: How the cook calculates
instruction: A processor can do nothing except connect gates. Using the allowed gates, build a circuit that matches the table. You get a star for the smallest number of gates.

levels.story: The cook needs to know whether two bits are the same. Output E lights up when A and B have the same value.
levels.why: XOR lights up when the bits differ. NOT flips that. This is how a processor compares numbers bit by bit.

levels.story: Add two bits. Output S is the digit of the result, output C is the carry to the next place, just like when you add 5 + 7 on paper.
levels.why: 1 + 1 = 10 in binary: digit 0 and carry 1. This circuit is called a half adder, and it’s the first step of every calculator.

levels.story: The cook reaches onto the worktop for one of two things. The control bit S says which one: S = 0 picks A, S = 1 picks B.

outputs.Y: (A and not S) or (B and S)

levels.why: This circuit is called a multiplexer. Choosing a cell in working memory is built from lots of these switches: the address decides which place gets read.

levels.story: Three temperature sensors vote on whether the processor is overheating. Output M lights up when at least two sensors light up. That way one broken sensor can’t set anything off.

outputs.M: (A and B) or (C and (A or B))

levels.why: Majority voting is a trick of reliable machines: space probes have three computers and trust the majority. The straightforward solution (A and B) or (A and C) or (B and C) needs 5 gates, a cleverer one only 4.

levels.story: Real addition: besides bits A and B, a carry C also comes in from the lower place. Build a full adder with outputs S and carry K.

outputs.K: (A and B) or (C and (A xor B))

levels.why: You use the gate A xor B twice: for the sum and for the carry. If you connect 64 of these adders in a row, you have an adder for 64-bit numbers, like in the processor of your phone.

debrief: The cook from the core “Inside a device” is really billions of gates. Comparing, adding and picking from memory are all made of the same little bricks. Carry on at nandgame.com, where you build a whole computer from them.
